cases.customer_question: Can additional products be added without a new Bluetooth SIG qualification when they use the same Bluetooth module and host stack as an already registered product?
question_variants: Can a derivative product be added for free?
Do similar products require a new Bluetooth registration?
Can I add another medical device using the same Bluetooth design?
What qualifies as a Product List addition?
Can multiple products share the same Bluetooth qualification?
cases.actual_issue: Determining eligibility for adding future products to an existing Bluetooth SIG Product List by reusing the same qualified Bluetooth architecture.
cases.plain_english_explanation: A company may release multiple products that use the same Bluetooth implementation. If the Bluetooth module and host stack remain unchanged, it may be possible to reuse the existing qualification rather than performing a new registration. Understanding this distinction can significantly reduce qualification effort.
cases.consultant_answer: The consultant explained that products implementing the same Bluetooth module and the same host stack can be added as derivative products under the existing registration. These products can be added through Product List management rather than requiring a completely new qualification registration. The consultant also recommended choosing a broad Design Name that can accommodate future product variants.
cases.decision_logic: Qualification reuse is permitted when the Bluetooth implementation remains unchanged. The determining factor is reuse of the same qualified module and host-stack architecture rather than the commercial product category itself.
cases.final_recommendation: When planning multiple products based on the same Bluetooth implementation, structure the initial registration to support future Product List additions and use a Design Name broad enough to cover future derivative models.
cases.risk_if_done_wrong: Misunderstanding derivative-product eligibility can result in unnecessary new registrations, avoidable qualification effort, and additional administrative work for products that could have reused the existing qualification.
